name: iPhone SE case with LEGO studs
design_notes: Target: iPhone SE 2nd/3rd gen (2020/2022), 138.4 x 67.3 x 7.3 mm, assumed corner radius ~9 mm. World frame: phone centred on origin, length along Y (+Y = top), phone back rests on z = back_t, screen faces +Z. Case back outer face at z=0; a 4 x stud_ny grid of LEGO studs (d 4.8, h 1.7, pitch 8.0 per LEGO standard), centred on the back, protrudes in -Z so the case presses onto LEGO plates/bricks. The 4 columns are sketched circles; change row count with stud_ny. Rigid-plastic snap fit: the top and bottom end walls and lip are removed between the corners by a U-shaped cut (end_open_w wide, down to the floor with root_r radii built into the profile for crack resistance), so the long side walls act as springs and the corner hooks plus lip_w lip retain the phone. end_open_w is kept 1 mm per side inside the corner tangent lines so the hook end faces sit on the flat end wall (edges on the tangent line cannot be filleted). Outer edges of the end openings and button slots are rounded with open_r (limited to ~0.4 mm by the 0.6 mm of end face left above the 1 mm back chamfer). Insert one long side first, then press the other side in. If it is too stiff, reduce lip_w or widen end_open_w; if it is loose, increase lip_w. Back chamfer excludes the studs. Button/camera positions are approximate; check against your phone before printing. Print orientation: studs on the bed with support under the back plate.

Remove the top and bottom end walls and lip between the corners (down to the back floor, with root_r radii into the floor for crack resistance) so the long side walls can spread and snap over a phone in rigid plastic; the bottom opening also clears the Lightning port, speaker and mic. Cut runs the full length but only removes material at the two ends; the middle of that zone is already the phone pocket
Break the outer back edge and camera opening edge; studs deliberately excluded so they keep a crisp LEGO fit
